blocks.text: READ: Follow Inquirer Sports’ special coverage of the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games 2026 TOKYO — Kayla Sanchez knows heartbreak can arrive in milliseconds. For Sanchez, it came after a blistering, national record-breaking swim that still left her just outside the podium at the Asian Games 2026. But what comes next is not retreat or regret, but a meticulously plotted rise toward the biggest stage of all–the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. “I allow myself to be sad and to be angry, but at a swim meet you don’t have much time,” said Sanchez, whose 24.75-second swim here placed her fourth in the women’s […]...
